source_title: Dynamic Effects of Applied Homofermentative Lactobacilli on Wet Grass Silage with Regard to Fermentation Quality and Mass Losses
authors: Reinhard Resch; Sonja Axmann; Elisabeth Weidenholzer; Ewald Kramer
source_type: Conference proceedings abstract reporting a primary experiment and Table 9
source_table_page: Table 9; proceedings section titled with the source title
license: No explicit dataset or proceedings reuse license identified in the retrieved document; verify reuse terms before redistribution outside this repository.
material_scope: First-growth permanent grassland (>95% grasses) at HBLFA Raumberg-Gumpenstein, Austria; harvested 2024-05-10; very slightly wilted grass at 238 g DM/kg fresh matter; untreated control versus a specific four-strain homofermentative LAB mixture.
experimental_conditions: Small vacuum bags were used for observations at 7 and 30 days; 60 L wide-neck barrels were used at 87 and 192 days. Ambient storage temperature was 10–18 °C. Forage was cut to 5–10 cm and was above 30 °C in the unloaded pile. The source describes 0.1–0.2 kg DM vacuum-bag samples in three replications and larger barrel fills. Table means are transcribed; no SD/SE is included in this extracted dataset.
applicability: Measured grass-silage evidence for storage duration, dry-matter concentration and loss, protein loss, ammonia-N, pH, metabolic energy, and fermentation products. It informs the possible direction and scale of anaerobic ensiling changes but is not roadside grass or the GreenHub loose-feed storage configuration.
limitations: Reference-only. Do not apply as a runtime default, universal kinetic law, fitted rate constant, aerobic degradation curve, or direct emissions factor. Only four storage durations are observed; vessel type changes between 30 and 87 days; temperature is a range; and the wet grass experienced challenging fermentation. Protein loss is source-calculated from nitrogen accounting and does not distinguish soluble and insoluble protein. No matched Dutch roadside-grass or commercial-scale validation is supplied.
conversion_or_processing: Transcribed treatment means from Table 9. Decimal comma 237,7 was normalized to 237.7. No interpolation, conversion, curve fitting, or missing-value imputation was performed. Blank cells remain unreported values.
rights_note: The source PDF is publicly accessible at the proceedings URL, but no explicit open-data license was located. The CSV contains a limited factual extraction, not source prose or the table image.
